title: SMART’s airport test puts human override before AI control
teaser: SMART, a proposed AI system for managing airspace, routes and trajectories, is headed for a first “soft launch” at an extremely busy airport in the Washington metropolitan area. Todd Sheridan Yiri, a former air traffic controller, says the aviation community still does not know what the system is meant to do: forecast conditions, or replace human decisions with air-traffic instructions. That distinction matters, because an AI tool that recommends actions is one risk; one that resolves conflicts at a crowded airport is another.
